statement: Provenance is an end-to-end traceable requirements lifecycle framework.
description:
The lifecycle has these stages: a Source, a Requirement, a Rule, the code, the test, review and the coverage scan. A Source records the material that an obligation comes from. A Requirement records an obligation of the system, and a Requirement can refine a different Requirement. A Rule records one behavioural obligation of a Requirement.

A rule marker connects the code to a Rule, and a test marker connects a test to a Rule. A person accepts or rejects each change to the graph on the review page. The coverage scan shows each active Rule that has no implementation or no verification. Each other Requirement in the default scope refines this Requirement through one or more parents.

Example: a person adds a project document as a Source. An agent and the person shape the document into a Requirement and a Rule. The person accepts the Rule on the review page. A developer adds a rule marker to the code and a test marker to a test. The coverage scan shows that the Rule has an implementation and a verification.
